deployment_audit.basis: SCHEDULE fields at lanes=1024, charged with the cycle model's own _compute_cycles

machine.rule: a DMA operator costs tiles x max(ceil(bytes_transferred / tiles / bytes_per_cycle), tile_issue_cycles); at this rate every tile of these deployments is at the issue floor, so the DMA charge is the tile count

deployment_audit.rule: compare, per engine family and per operator, every SCHEDULE field runtime.cycle.model.tile_mapping reads, the tile counts and padding those fields produce for the same useful work at the same request, and for DMA the tile count and bytes per tile; comparable only when no cost-bearing field differs outside the cited allowlist

tensor_parity_band.note: rates on which the two depths are charged alike per unit of depth; the machine rate sits inside it

deployment_audit.verdict: NOT COMPARABLE: 5 further cost-bearing field(s) differ (bank_mask; see asymmetries); allowlist empty.  These are SCHEDULE fields, so no machine file can correct them; the deployments must be re-emitted under one SCHEDULE rule.

deployment_audit_under_proposed_allowlis.verdict: COMPARABLE: 26 operators matched operator-for-operator with identical SCHEDULE fields in every family (55 fields compared); tiles per step equal in every family; 5 allowlisted difference(s), all cited.  The machine files alone decide the rate.

proposed_allowlist.attention.bank_mask: AM-C4 (docs/CHIP_ARCHITECTURE_DESIGN.md section 3.8; section 10.1 AM-C4; section 7.1 rows 1-2): bank_mask bit b = bank group b of the storage class of the operator's streamed operand, and the two chips stream from different stores -- mask-ROM banks on the ROM chip (configs/hardware/abi3_capability/rom_qwen3.json memory.rom.banks; RomProgramBuilder._bank_mask names the weight input's mask-ROM shards, 0 when the operator reads no ROM operand; checked by compiler/backends/rom/common/check.py rom_bank_mask), scratchpad staging bank groups 0-7 on the HBM chip (compiler/backends/hbm_sram/lower.py _ENGINE_REGIONS; plan.py _allocate_sram).  Caveat: runtime/cycle/model.py MemorySystem.schedule applies bank_mask to SRAM-class accesses only, so the ROM side's ROM-bank bits confine its scratchpad accesses to same-indexed SRAM banks -- a cycle-model semantics defect (a ROM-store mask applied to the scratchpad) that AM-C4 does not remove and that the AM-E9 re-emission does not fix.
